Create Transition-Predictor Relationship Table

Source: R/trans_preds_t.R
trans_preds_t.Rd

Creates a trans_preds_t table, which lists the transition / predictor pairs a run considers. is_selected says which of them the transition models use: feature selection sets it to FALSE for the predictors it prunes. Further columns, such as the scores of get_pred_filter_score(), are added to the table as they are written; they are for reporting only. When writing a selection back, assign the scored table with its flags rather than a subset of it: rows left out of the assignment keep the flags they had.

Usage

as_trans_preds_t(x)

# S3 method for class 'trans_preds_t'
print(x, nrow = 10, ...)

set_full_trans_preds(self, reset = FALSE)

get_pred_filter_score(
  self,
  filter = "correlation",
  id_trans = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A list or data.frame coercible to a trans_preds_t object. If missing, an empty table will be created. If it has no is_selected column, every pair is selected.

nrow

see data.table::print.data.table

...

Additional arguments passed to flt if filter is a character string

self

An evoland_db instance with populated trans_meta_t and pred_meta_t tables

reset

Bool, start the active run's selection over? This removes the active run's rows, including their score columns' values, before writing the full set.

filter

An mlr3filters::Filter object or a character string specifying the filter method, retrieved via mlr3filters::flt. Note that your filter must be compatible with the feature data types; compare your pred_meta_t table to https://mlr3filters.mlr-org.com for filter compatibility.

id_trans

Optional integer vector of transition IDs; only these transitions are scored. NULL (default) scores every transition with selected predictors.

cluster

An optional cluster object, see run_parallel_evoland

Value

A data.table of class "trans_preds_t" with columns:

  • id_run: Foreign key to runs_t

  • id_pred: Foreign key to pred_meta_t

  • id_trans: Foreign key to trans_meta_t

  • is_selected: Logical, whether the models of the transition use the predictor

  • any further columns, e.g. filter scores

Methods (by generic)

  • print(trans_preds_t): Print a trans_preds_t object, passing params to data.table print

Functions

  • set_full_trans_preds(): Set an initial full set of transition / predictor relations for the active run: every predictor for every viable transition, all selected

  • get_pred_filter_score(): Get a filter score for the selected transition-predictor relationships based on mlr3filters. Returns trans_preds_t with an additional column named after the filter$id. The filter score can be used for feature selection: set is_selected according to the score and write the table back, e.g. scores[, is_selected := importance > 100]; db$trans_preds_t <- scores. Writing it back also stores the scores. Only the selected pairs are scored, so a second filter refines the selection of the first.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# a typical selection step
scores <- db$get_pred_filter_score("importance")
scores[, is_selected := importance > 100]
db$trans_preds_t <- scores
} # }
